overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: CAOS LDA HSI explores what probabilistic topic models can capture when documents are pixels, regions, or measurements drawn from hyperspectral imagery.

landing_cta.lead: Probabilistic topic models on hyperspectral imagery — a multi-axis evaluation framework that asks whether LDA basis spectra add interpretable value over deep encoders for HSI scene classification.

hero.title: We treat every hyperspectral pixel as a document.
hero.caption: Each curve is the mean signature of one agronomic class in the Indian Pines cube. The inter-class diversity at 1100 / 1400 / 1900 nm — water and feldspar absorptions — is what the textual corpus has to recover discretely. That signature is a document; the project's question is which topics (shared latent structure) live in it.
hero.datacube_caption: An HSI cube is (H × W × B). Each pixel x[i, j] is a B-band spectral vector. The project walks it as a corpus, discretises it into tokens, fits topics θ ∈ Δ^(K-1) and compares them against K-dim baselines.

papers.section_lead: Both PDFs below are preprints — current build of the manuscripts as of the most recent deploy. They have not been submitted to a peer-reviewed venue yet; treat them as work-in-progress.

journal.title: Probabilistic topic models on hyperspectral imagery
journal.blurb: Long-form treatment: 12-axis Framework, hierarchical Bayesian benchmarks, deep-encoder ablations, HIDSAG cross-preprocessing stability.
journal.note: Preprint; target venue redacted while it circulates.

conference.title: Topic-routed classifiers for hyperspectral scene labelling
conference.blurb: Short companion: theta-as-gate vs theta-as-feature, the B-3 result, and the multi-axis battery summary.
conference.note: Preprint; target venue redacted while it circulates.

b3.title: θ as a gate beats θ as a feature; small lift over raw
b3.body: topic_routed_soft ties or narrowly beats raw_logistic on 4 of 6 labelled scenes (mean lift ≈ +0.5–1.5 pp; Pavia U is the largest at +1.4 pp). The bigger story is theta_logistic (θ as a flat feature), which loses to raw by 14 pp (Pavia U) up to 47 pp (Indian Pines). The 'θ is a gate, not a feature' framing is empirically validated.

b3_followup.title: No deep encoder can replace θ as the gate
b3_followup.body: Hierarchical Bayesian: raw > θ > {pca_8, cae_1d_8, beta_vae_8} at P(μ_a > μ_b) ≥ 0.999. Softmaxed deep latents satisfy the simplex constraint geometrically but not structurally — the gating mechanism does not transfer.

topic_family.title: LDA wins ARI · ProdLDA wins coherence · ETM is the safe middle
topic_family.body: Head-to-head on 220-per-class stratified samples: LDA wins KMeans-vs-label ARI on 4/6 scenes (loses to ProdLDA/ETM on Pavia U and KSC); ProdLDA wins c_v topic coherence 6/6; ETM beats ProdLDA on ARI 5/6 (KSC is a tie at 0.222 vs 0.223; ETM wins the other five).

decoder_design.title: Decoder reconstruction target is itself a hyperparameter
decoder_design.body: CAE-3D anchor-only vs full-patch gives net mean ΔARI ≈ +0.003 (K=8) and +0.011 (K=4) — neutral on average, scene-dependent direction. Pavia U inverts with capacity.

gpu_stack.title: 50–120× speedup on the deep / neural family
gpu_stack.body: RTX 4070 Laptop CUDA 12.6: cae_3d_full K=32 single scene goes from ~60 min CPU to ~30 s GPU. Full K-curve {4, 8, 16, 32} × 6 scenes from 9–12 h CPU to ~10 min GPU. Determinism drift ±0.010 ARI is below per-seed σ ≈ 0.05. Engineering claim — runtime / determinism only, not a methodological result.

stability.title: 9-method × 6-scene seed stability ladder
stability.body: PCA = ICA (1.000 deterministic) > LDA > NMF > CAE-2D > CAE-1D > CAE-3D > dense-AE > β-VAE. KSC β-VAE off-diag ≈ 0.18 — KL stochasticity overwhelms the inter-seed signal.

posterior_collapse.title: β-VAE Salinas at β ≥ 8 — textbook failure mode
posterior_collapse.body: Salinas β-VAE at β=8 and β=16 collapses to ARI = 0.000: the encoder converges to q(z|x) ≈ p(z) regardless of input; the latent is uninformative. Salinas-A's compact 6-class structure resists the same regulariser.

pipeline_anatomy.title: From the HSI cube to θ ∈ Δ^(K-1)
pipeline_anatomy.lead: Four steps that the app serves pre-computed behind every /api/topic-views/{scene} endpoint: define document, discretise to tokens, fit the model, inspect the per-pixel θ mixture.
pipeline_anatomy.stage1_note: x ∈ ℝᴮ per pixel · region · sample

scenes.title: Each scene with its class distribution
scenes.lead: Each bar is one agronomic / urban / mineral class with its real relative frequency. KSC and Botswana are tough benchmarks (diluted majority class, low SNR).

pillars.title: Any topic result is attributable to these three levers
pillars.documents_body: How to build a document: by pixel, by region (SLIC, Felzenszwalb), by patch or by full sample. Four alternatives materialised in build_groupings; they change the statistical unit upstream.
pillars.discretisation_body: How a continuous spectrum becomes a discrete token: twelve recipes V1..V12, three quantisation schemes (uniform, quantile, equalised), three levels Q ∈ {8, 16, 32}.
pillars.model_body: Canonical LDA (collapsed Gibbs, variational Bayes, online), HDP, CTM, ProdLDA, ETM, NMF, PCA, ICA, dense-AE, CAE-1D/2D/3D, β-VAE — all at the same K for a fair comparison.

coverage.title: 11 + 5 + 4 + 12 axes — all evaluated on the same scene when applicable

index.lead: Four entries: the theory behind the model, the representations the corpus accepts, the pipeline that produces the data, and how topics are applied to downstream tasks.
index.reading: Suggested reading: Theory → Representations → Pipeline → Application. The Bayesian Method Comparison and Multi-Axis Addendum B wiki pages close the methodological loop.
index.theory_body: The probabilistic topic model (PTM) and why an HSI pixel can be treated as a document. LDA in plate notation, variational inference, generalisations to HDP and CTM.
index.repr_body: Twelve wordification recipes (V1 band → V12 GMM-token), three schemes (uniform/quantile/equalised), Q ∈ {8, 16, 32}. Plus five deep encoders: CAE-1D / CAE-2D / CAE-3D anchor and full-patch / β-VAE. PCA, NMF, ICA as fair K-dim baselines.
index.pipe_body: Diagram of the 12 stages of the data-pipeline: fetch_* (acquire) → research_core (paths/loaders) → build_* (offline compute) → curate_for_web → manifest. Five torch builders detect GPU automatically with CPU fallback.
index.app_body: How topics are applied to downstream tasks: flat feature (theta_logistic, dominated by raw), gating (topic_routed_soft = soft mixture of per-topic specialists, matches or beats raw 6/6), embedded (concat [θ | pca_K], small effect on IP). The B-3 follow-up closes: the Dirichlet simplex matters, not K-dim compression.

why-ptm.title: What is a probabilistic topic model?
why-ptm.lead: A probabilistic topic model (PTM) describes every document as a latent mixture over a handful of word distributions called topics. The key point is that this latent structure is learned without supervision from word co-occurrences alone.

lda-plate.title: LDA — plate notation and generative process
lda-plate.lead: The outer plates repeat over documents and words; the latent distributions (theta and phi) are the objects the model learns.

hsi-as-document.title: HSI as a corpus — why a pixel can be a document
hsi-as-document.lead: Each pixel of a hyperspectral image is a reflectance vector. For LDA to consume it, the spectrum must be quantised and turned into a discrete sequence of tokens.

why-mixed-membership.title: Mixed membership — why not hard classification?
why-mixed-membership.lead: The spectrum of a mineral pixel does not come from a single species. Mixtures, intermixed vegetation, shadow and atmospheric scattering yield measurements that reflect several signatures at once.

topics-vs-endmembers.title: Topics vs endmembers — the φ ↔ E relationship
topics-vs-endmembers.lead: Linear spectral unmixing factorises a cube into endmember signatures × per-pixel abundances. LDA factorises a tokenised cube into topic distributions × per-document mixtures. The two factorisations are different objects, but on mineral scenes they end up describing the same underlying material families — which is why the per-topic cosine vs endmember runs 0.7–0.9 on the HIDSAG mineral subsets.

coherence-metrics.title: Topic coherence — c_v, NPMI, and U-Mass
coherence-metrics.lead: Coherence quantifies whether the top words of a topic 'go together' in the corpus. The three metrics this project tracks (c_v, NPMI, U-Mass) measure that signal at different scales and with different statistics. Higher is better for c_v and NPMI; less-negative is better for U-Mass.

metric-glossary.title: Metric glossary — partition agreement, spectral angle, β
metric-glossary.lead: Three definitions referenced throughout the site that the prior surfaces named but never gave on-page. Each is a one-line formula plus the role it plays in the framework.

methodology_representations.title: Representations · method-by-method
methodology_representations.lead: Each method (16 total — 5 classical topic models + 2 neural topic models + 4 K-dim baselines + 5 deep encoders + 1 unmixing) has its own theoretical formulation, design principles, starting hypothesis, and findings against the 6 labelled scenes. Pick a method to drill in.
methodology_representations.recipes_lead: Topic-family methods operate on a discrete word alphabet. The project ships 12 wordification recipes (V1..V12) × 3 quantisation schemes × Q ∈ {8, 16, 32} = 108 configs per scene. The grid below sketches the space. The canonical recipe is V1 (band-frequency, band-as-word) with uniform Q=8.
methodology_representations.recipes_figure_caption: 12 recipes × 9 (3 schemes × 3 Q) = 108 configs per scene.

lda.label: LDA · online VB
lda.theory_body: Latent Dirichlet Allocation models each document as a mixture θ_d over K topics. Each token w_{d,n} is generated by first drawing a topic z_{d,n} with probability θ_d, then a word with probability φ_{z_{d,n}}. Online variational inference (Hoffman–Blei–Bach 2010) uses mini-batches and stochastic VI.
principles: K is fixed a priori (K = n_classes by project convention).
Canonical priors from the Procemin/A39 paper: α = 0.45, η = 0.2.
Canonical recipe V1 (band-frequency, band-as-word) with Q ∈ {8, 16, 32}.
lda.hypothesis: If a hyperspectral image is a corpus of pixels-as-documents, the discrete topics discovered should align with labelled agronomic/mineral classes.
lda.findings: Wins ARI on 4/6 scenes (Indian Pines, Salinas, Salinas-A, Pavia U) vs ProdLDA and ETM in head-to-head; loses 1/6 in KSC where it collapses to ARI≈0; loses 1/6 in Botswana vs ETM. Coherence c_v 0/6 (always worst). σ ≤ 0.03 ARI over N=5 seeds — extremely stable.

lda_tomo.label: LDA · tomotopy (collapsed Gibbs)
lda_tomo.theory_body: Collapsed: integrates φ and θ analytically and leaves only the discrete topic assignments z as Gibbs variables. Iteration i: re-sample z_i conditional on the rest. Slower (10× online VB) but usually finds better local maxima.
principles: No variational gap — the sampler distribution converges to the true posterior.
Burn-in + N effective iterations; per-document log-likelihood as diagnostic.
C++ implementation via tomotopy → 50× faster than pure-Python Gibbs.
lda_tomo.hypothesis: A better φ estimator should translate to more semantically coherent topics (higher c_v).
lda_tomo.findings: Wins coherence c_v on 4/6 scenes vs online LDA. Coherence-vs-ARI tradeoff: tomotopy is strong on c_v, but ARI vs label stays similar. Use it when interpretability is the priority.

lda_sparse.label: LDA · sparse VB
lda_sparse.theory_body: Same as online LDA but with α = 0.05 (Dirichlet mode pushed towards simplex vertices). θ_d becomes peaked: each document concentrates on few topics.
principles: Strict sparsity prior: documents with only 1–3 active topics.
Useful when classes are disjoint (agronomic classes don't mix within a pixel).
Perplexity usually worse — but better fit for categorical labels.
lda_sparse.hypothesis: Higher sparsity should improve ARI vs label (every document → one clear dominant topic).
lda_sparse.findings: Worse perplexity than canonical LDA, marginally worse ARI in most scenes. Confirms that for HSI data, pixels are not single-topic.

hdp.label: HDP · tomotopy
hdp.theory_body: HDP (Teh–Jordan–Beal–Blei 2006) is the non-parametric extension of LDA: the number of topics K is learned from the corpus via stick-breaking. Topics are shared across documents via a hierarchical Dirichlet process.
principles: K is not fixed a priori — the model decides how many active topics exist.
Truncation T (upper cap) for tractable inference; T = 50 typical.
Useful when there's no prior on n_classes (unlabelled scenes).
hdp.hypothesis: For scenes with unknown class count, HDP should auto-identify the effective K and converge to coherent topics.
hdp.findings: On the 6 labelled scenes, HDP typically activates 8–15 effective topics (n_classes ∈ {9, 13, 16}). c_v comparable to LDA. ARI vs label competitive with LDA when the learned K is close to the true one.

ctm.label: CTM · tomotopy
ctm.theory_body: Blei–Lafferty 2007. Replaces the Dirichlet prior with a logistic-normal: η_d ∈ ℝ^{K-1} with non-diagonal covariance Σ. Softmax converts η to θ. Σ encodes topic correlations.
principles: Relaxes the topic independence that LDA imposes via the Dirichlet.
Inference more expensive (logistic-normal is not conjugate with multinomial).
Σ is an additional free parameter with K(K-1)/2 entries.
ctm.hypothesis: For HSI, spectrally neighbouring topics may correlate (e.g. early- and late-stage vegetation share bands). CTM should capture this.
ctm.findings: Compute time 5–10× LDA. Marginal ARI gain (<0.02). Off-diagonal Σ is not structurally informative on the tested corpora.

prodlda.label: ProdLDA · Pyro
prodlda.theory_body: Neural topic model: an MLP encoder amortises z inference, the decoder is a multinomial softmax over β = K×V. ELBO with Dirichlet KL via Laplace approximation.
principles: Neural encoder + decoder — gradient training over the full corpus.
Topic coherence c_v typically better than LDA (the decoder learns band-relations).
Init-sensitive: σ(ARI) ≈ 0.03 across N=5 seeds.
prodlda.hypothesis: Amortised encoder should match LDA on ARI and improve c_v thanks to the neural decoder.
prodlda.findings: Wins c_v 6/6 scenes vs LDA and ETM. Loses ARI 4/6 vs LDA and 6/6 vs ETM under N=5 multi-seed estimation (cycle 63). Confirms the explicit tradeoff: coherence vs discriminability. Operational rule: ProdLDA for interpretability, LDA for clustering.

etm.label: ETM · Embedded Topic Model
etm.theory_body: Factorised decoder: β = ρα^T where ρ ∈ ℝ^{V×E} are word embeddings and α ∈ ℝ^{K×E} are topic embeddings. E ≪ V accelerates and regularises. Variational gaussian over θ.
principles: Low-rank decoder E ≤ 256 — captures semantic similarity between words (neighbouring bands).
Word embeddings ρ are learned jointly with topics.
Better for large vocabularies; HSI has V ≈ 200 bands.
etm.hypothesis: A shared word embedding should help when there's spectral redundancy (correlated bands).
etm.findings: ETM > ProdLDA on ARI 6/6 scenes under N=5 multi-seed estimation (cycle 63 — the single-seed ProdLDA-on-KSC win disappears with variance). Coherence c_v in the middle: ProdLDA > ETM > LDA. ETM is the best ARI+c_v compromise.

nmf.label: NMF · K=8
nmf.theory_body: Non-negative matrix factorisation. β-divergence = KL. W ∈ ℝ_+^{N×K} are per-document scores, H ∈ ℝ_+^{K×V} are basis spectra. Multiplicative update rules.
principles: Parts-based: every spectrum is a non-negative sum of K basis spectra.
No stochastic priors — deterministic solution (init-dependent).
Direct K-dim baseline against LDA / PCA / AE at the same K.
nmf.hypothesis: If spectral mixing is physically linear, NMF should recover endmembers comparable to NFINDR.
nmf.findings: Reconstruction RMSE comparable to PCA at K=8. Silhouette and ARI vs label worse than PCA on 4/6 scenes — NMF components are more interpretable than separable.

pca.label: PCA · K=8
pca.theory_body: Eigendecomposition of the covariance C ∈ ℝ^{V×V}. Top-K eigenvectors form the basis V_{:K}. The projection z_d = V_{:K}^T x_d is L2-optimal in reconstruction (Eckart–Young).
principles: Linear compression — preserves maximum variance in K directions.
Reconstruction RMSE is minimal at every K (its only guaranteed title).
Components can be negative — no direct physical interpretation.
pca.hypothesis: For HSI data dominated by a single brightness direction of variance, PCA should be a hard baseline to beat on MSE but poor on separability.
pca.findings: Wins reconstruction RMSE at every tested K (4, 8, 12, 16, 32). Silhouette intermediate. ARI vs label moderate. It is the canonical L2 baseline against which every deep encoder must justify itself.

ica.label: ICA · K=8 (FastICA)
ica.theory_body: Independent Component Analysis. Assumes x = As with statistically independent (non-Gaussian) sources s. FastICA uses kurtosis / negentropy. ν ~ N(0,1) is the Gaussian reference.
principles: Statistical independence > decorrelation (PCA).
Useful when distinguishable physical sources exist (water, vegetation, soil).
Slower convergence than PCA but comparable cost overall.
ica.hypothesis: If HSI is a mixture of few independent physical sources, ICA should recover them better than PCA in silhouette.
ica.findings: Latents comparable to PCA in ARI/NMI. Silhouette slightly lower on 3/6 scenes — ICA components capture different structure but not necessarily more separable.

dense_ae.label: Dense AE · K=8
dense_ae.theory_body: Linear neural baseline. MLP encoder → bottleneck K, symmetric MLP decoder. MSE loss. No convolution, no recurrence. Equivalent to non-linear PCA.
principles: Non-linear generalisation of PCA at the same K.
GPU-trained (project cycles 59+).
No additional regularisation (no KL, no dropout) — comparable to PCA in degenerate cases.
dense_ae.hypothesis: For low K (4, 8), non-linear relations between bands should give better reconstruction than PCA.
dense_ae.findings: Reconstruction RMSE comparable to PCA (not better at K=8 averaged over 6 scenes). Silhouette and ARI slightly worse than PCA — the model learns the same as PCA but with more seed variance.

cae_1d.label: CAE-1D · K=8
cae_1d.theory_body: 1D convolutional AE over the spectrum. Kernel = 7 adjacent bands. Encoder = 3 Conv1D layers + 2 dense, bottleneck K = 8.
principles: Assumes local structure in the spectrum (neighbouring bands correlated).
Receptive field grows exponentially with depth — captures wider features.
Stride 2 between layers progressively reduces the spectral dimension.
cae_1d.hypothesis: Hyperspectral spectra have band-to-band autocorrelation. CAE-1D should capture local features (edges, peaks) better than PCA/dense AE.
cae_1d.findings: Sits mid-ladder in the 9-method seed-stability ranking (below LDA / NMF / CAE-2D, above CAE-3D / dense-AE / β-VAE — see README headline #6). Silhouette comparable to PCA. The 1D conv inductive bias on band-to-band autocorrelation makes it the deep encoder closest to PCA on the ARI / σ tradeoff.

cae_2d.label: CAE-2D · K=8 (anchor)
cae_2d.theory_body: 2D CAE over P×P×B patches (P=7 spatial pixels × B bands). Conv2D encoder + bottleneck K=8 just for the centre pixel of the patch.
principles: Captures spatial texture (not just the spectral profile).
Anchor mode: only the patch centre contributes to loss and to z.
Spatial neighbourhood = 3.5 pixels effective radius.
cae_2d.hypothesis: Spatial context should improve separability — an agricultural pixel surrounded by agricultural pixels is easier to classify.
cae_2d.findings: At N=15 seeds: ARI vs label competitive with CAE-1D. Better on scenes with clear textures (Indian Pines), worse on fine mosaics (Salinas-A).

cae_3d.label: CAE-3D anchor · K=8
cae_3d.theory_body: Conv3D over full cubes (spatial × spectral dimension). 3D kernels = (3 bands × 3 px × 3 px). Anchor: only the centre pixel defines z.
principles: Volumetric receptive field — captures spatial and spectral neighbourhood simultaneously.
More compute-expensive — GPU training 50–120× via CUDA.
Anchor mode reduces loss noise by focusing on the target pixel.
cae_3d.hypothesis: Conv3D should be strictly better than CAE-2D + CAE-1D combined — more native inductive capacity.
cae_3d.findings: K-curve {K=4, K=8} neutral: ΔARI K=4 = +0.011 (5/6 scenes confirm direction); Pavia U inverts with capacity. Not a decisive gain over CAE-1D — volumetric capacity is not the dominant lever.

cae_3d_full.label: CAE-3D full · K=8
cae_3d_full.theory_body: Same net as CAE-3D anchor, but the loss penalises every pixel of the P×P patch (not only the centre). Uses more signal per gradient step.
principles: Dense loss (P² more pixels contribute) reduces gradient noise.
K-dim embedding per pixel computed at inference.
GPU-trained; same architecture as anchor, different loss.
cae_3d_full.hypothesis: Dense loss should give cleaner gradients and more stable latents.
cae_3d_full.findings: Equivalent to anchor on ARI vs label at N=15 across 6 scenes. Not decisively better on any scene. Cycle 58 confirmed identical K-curve between anchor and full.

beta_vae.label: β-VAE · K=8
beta_vae.tag: Higgins et al. 2017 · β KL term
beta_vae.theory_body: Variational AE with β multiplier on the KL term. β = 1 ⇒ standard VAE. β > 1 forces z dimensions to be more independent (disentangled).
principles: Probabilistic latent — z is a distribution, not a point.
β controls the reconstruction-vs-disentanglement tradeoff.
Canonical default here: β = 2.
beta_vae.hypothesis: A disentangled latent should help interpretability without sacrificing much reconstruction.
beta_vae.findings: At β = 2, comparable to CAE-1D on ARI/NMI. β-sweep over β ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} (cycle 42 5-β grid) shows documented collapse at β ≥ 8 (KL → 0, only the prior remains). β = 2 is the sweet spot.

endmember.label: Endmembers · NFINDR + NNLS
endmember.theory_body: NFINDR (Winter 1999): K endmembers are the vertices of the maximum-volume simplex in the HSI cube. NNLS with sum-to-one constraint (delta = 100 penalty) infers per-pixel abundance.
principles: Linear mixing model — every pixel = convex sum of K endmembers.
Physically interpretable: every endmember is a candidate pure material.
Compared against LDA via topic_endmember_match: K-K cosine matrix.
endmember.hypothesis: If HSI pixels are linear combinations of few pure materials, LDA topics should align with endmembers.
endmember.findings: Best per-topic cosine vs NFINDR/ATGP endmembers on the six public labelled scenes sits in the 0.94–1.00 range on five of six (Indian Pines, Salinas, Salinas-A, Pavia U, Botswana); KSC drops to a 0.58–1.00 spread, suggesting one topic without a clean linear endmember match. The HIDSAG-mineral endmember comparison is part of the planned F-12 deepening and is not yet shipped.

overview.title: Overview
overview.lead: Twelve chained stages. Each is a single-command script. Each stage's output is the input for the next.

stages.title: The stages, command by command
stages.lead: The commands assume you are at the repo root and have the two venvs created (scripts/local setup-all).

spatial-coherence.title: Spatial coherence — what the groupings stage measures
spatial-coherence.lead: The four document constructions (SLIC-500, SLIC-2000, patch-7/15, Felzenszwalb) carve the cube in geometrically different ways. The cross-method agreement panel summarises how often they place two pixels in the same document; the per-method spatial-coherence diagnostics summarise how compact each construction's regions are.

reproduce.title: How to reproduce the full corpus

boundary.title: What the web app does NOT do

methodology_application.title: Application to classification and regression via topics

why.title: Why not classify directly?
why.lead: Reducing an HSI cube to hard classes throws away all the mixture information. If a pixel is 60% soil and 40% scrub, a hard label picks one and lies. Topics preserve the mixture.

three-families.title: Three families of topic-based models
three-families.lead: Each family uses theta in a different way. The difference is methodological, not cosmetic.

direct.title: 1. Direct — theta as feature
direct.lead: The simplest, also the least informative.

routed.title: 2. Routed — one specialist per topic
routed.lead: Each topic trains its own classifier on the raw spectrum, weighted by membership.

embedded.title: 3. Embedded — theta concatenated with baseline
embedded.lead: Concat is the least elegant but sometimes the healthiest: let the classifier decide how much theta weighs.

regression.title: Regression over measurements (HIDSAG)
regression.lead: When the target is not a class but a continuous measurement (Cu %, Au g/t, mineral grade), the logic is the same with linear regressors.

bayesian-spec.title: Hierarchical Bayesian benchmark — model spec
bayesian-spec.lead: The pairwise posterior probabilities P(μ_a > μ_b) above come from a flat one-way ANOVA-style model with additive scene and fold offsets, fit with PyMC NUTS. The spec below mirrors the actual code in build_bayesian_classification_labelled.py exactly — no hidden hyperpriors.

hungarian-stability.title: Hungarian topic-matching — stability and cross-mask identity
hungarian-stability.lead: Topic indices are not stable across re-fits — both LDA seeds and water-mask choices can permute the K topics. The seed-stability and cross-mask validation blocks pair topics by the assignment that maximises the average matched cosine. That is the Hungarian (linear-assignment) algorithm applied to a topic-cosine cost matrix.

paired-statistics.title: Paired statistics — Cliff δ, Wilcoxon-Holm, Friedman-Nemenyi
paired-statistics.lead: The Benchmarks page reports method-vs-method comparisons that use three non-parametric tools. Each is one paragraph here so the headline numbers (Cliff δ = +0.28 on the embedded baseline, P(routed_soft > raw) = 0.641, Wilcoxon-Holm < 0.05) are self-contained.

axis-crosswalk.title: F-axes (paper) ↔ B-axes (wiki / web app)
axis-crosswalk.lead: The companion paper introduces a twelve-axis Framework (F-1..F-12). This site and the wiki use a different B-1..B-12 taxonomy that predates the paper. The two share three concepts under different ordinals; the crosswalk below makes the mapping explicit.

what-topics-capture.title: What does a topic "capture", in task terms?
what-topics-capture.lead: It is not text: the question is answered visually with distributions.

databases.title: Databases
databases.lead: 21 datasets grouped in 4 families. Each declares modality, domains, supervision status, and whether it has local roots available for the pipeline. Raw data is not served from the web app — only the publishable derived artifacts.
databases.family_a_tagline: USGS / ECOSTRESS curves — reference spectra with label or measurement.
databases.family_b_tagline: AVIRIS / ROSIS / Hyperion cubes with pixel-level labels — Indian Pines, Salinas, Pavia U, KSC, Botswana.
databases.family_cd_tagline: HIDSAG geo-mining + MicaSense MSI — regions with physical or geochemical measurements.
databases.family_e_tagline: Cubes without reliable labels — Borsoi unmixing benchmarks (Samson, Jasper Ridge, Urban) with manual endmembers.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.lead: Guided flow in four steps: family → subset → representation → explore. Each step depends on the previous; you can go back at any time.

index.title: Methods workspace
index.lead: Explore each topic-modelling method on its own page: how the tokens are built, the theory hypothesis, the F-axis sweep, and side-by-side comparators. Twelve wordification recipes (V1..V12) plus four neural baselines.

deep.compare_lead: Jump to any other method to see its results side by side.
deep.no_sweep_yet: This method is a baseline; the V-sweep does not re-run it per recipe. Existing results from the V1 evaluation are surfaced elsewhere.
deep.sweep_pending: Sweep results appear here as the F-1, F-2, F-5 and remaining F-axes complete. The pipeline is running.

V1.title: Band-frequency tokens (V1)
V1.summary: Each band contributes one token (band, quantised intensity). The canonical recipe; doc length = B; the substrate used for every F-axis in the current paper.
V1.theory: The simplest faithful encoding: preserves both band identity and quantised intensity. Documents are dense (one token per band), so LDA can rediscover labelled-class spectra as topic-word distributions. Expected wins on F-1 classification and F-12 baselines on labelled landcover scenes; expected losses on F-9 HIDSAG preprocessing where the magnitude is the artefact, and on F-5 band-mask robustness when label boundaries are spatial-acquisition artefacts.

V2.title: Magnitude-only tokens (V2)
V2.summary: Drops band identity entirely; the document is the histogram of intensity bins. Tests whether band shape matters or only the intensity distribution.
V2.theory: The band-shuffled control: removes all spectral identity and keeps only the intensity histogram. Anywhere V2 wins, the spectrum is essentially shape-blind and V1's edge is illusory. Expect V2 to be a floor across F-axes; if it floats up on some scene, that is the strongest evidence that band identity is not informative there.

V3.title: Joint (band, bin) vocabulary (V3)
V3.summary: Larger vocab B × Q encoding intensity-specific band signatures. Wider design space than V1 at the cost of vocabulary size.
V3.theory: The source schematic called this a concat trigram (3-band context); the implementation is actually a joint (band, bin) Cartesian product. This larger vocabulary lets the topic basis encode intensity-specific band signatures at the cost of seed sensitivity (F-3) and a rate-distortion penalty (F-11). Expected to do well on F-2 where finer vocabulary aligns to topic-specific signatures.

V4.title: Slope-encoded tokens (V4)
V4.summary: Tokens encode local dλ. Robust to overall brightness or normalisation drift.
V4.theory: Slope features are invariant to multiplicative scaling and additive shifts of the spectrum, so V4 should be robust where V1 is fragile under band masking (F-5). Expected to underperform V1 on scenes where absolute reflectance is the diagnostic (Pavia U). Useful as a baseline against SAM-style literature.

V5.title: Curvature-encoded tokens (V5)
V5.summary: Tokens encode d²/dλ². Captures absorption-feature inflection points.
V5.theory: Curvature peaks correspond to inflection points of absorption features and are common in mineralogical preprocessing. Expected wins on HIDSAG (F-1, F-9). Caveat: high-frequency noise amplifies second differences, so F-3 seed stability may suffer.

V6.title: Wavelet coefficient tokens (V6)
V6.summary: Daubechies-4 wavelet decomposition; all coefficients binned. Multi-scale spectral structure.
V6.theory: Multi-scale captures both broad continuum and narrow absorption simultaneously. Expected wins on F-2 coherence (wavelet bands align to physical scales) and F-12 baselines (wavelet features are a classical HSI baseline). Risk: topics are basis-aligned rather than label-aligned, so F-7 topic-label coupling may degrade.

V7.title: Absorption-feature triplets (V7)
V7.summary: Continuum-removed spectrum via convex hull; up to 6 features per pixel as (centroid, depth, area). The most physically motivated recipe for mineralogy.
V7.theory: Each token is an actual absorption feature with measured centroid, depth and area. The most chemistry-faithful representation: it directly mirrors how spectroscopists read mineral spectra. Expected wins on HIDSAG F-1 (mineralogical separation), F-2 (topics aligned to USGS spectra) and F-7. Documents have at most six tokens, so K must be tightly bounded.

V8.title: Endmember-fraction tokens (V8)
V8.summary: NFINDR-precomputed endmembers; NNLS unmixing produces one token per endmember weighted by abundance.
V8.theory: Bakes the linear-mixing-model assumption into the tokens. Expected wins on Salinas where field-edge mixed pixels dominate, and F-12 against unmixing literature. Limit: seed stability (F-3) depends on which NFINDR endmembers were chosen, and NFINDR itself is seed-dependent.

V9.title: Region-SAM tokens (V9)
V9.summary: Felzenszwalb spatial pre-segmentation; each pixel emits one token (region_id, SAM-distance-to-region-mean).
V9.theory: Spatial aggregation damps band-level noise and bakes neighbourhood information into the corpus. Expected wins on F-5 band-mask robustness and F-3 seed stability (fewer tokens means less variance). Pays the price on F-1 pixel-resolution classification and F-11 rate-distortion.

V10.title: Physical band-group tokens (V10)
V10.summary: Hard partition into VNIR / SWIR-1 / SWIR-2. Three tokens per pixel encoding group means.
V10.theory: The coarsest spectral representation. Useful as a what-if-we-used-only-3-bands baseline; expected to lose most F-axes but provides a tight floor for comparison.

V11.title: Codebook-VQ tokens (V11)
V11.summary: Splits the B-vector into 4 sub-vectors; each sub-vector encoded as one of Q codewords learnt by k-means.
V11.theory: Standard product quantisation used in approximate-nearest-neighbour search, repurposed as a wordification. Expected wins on F-11 rate-distortion and F-12 against vector-quantisation literature. Reproducibility caveat: the current implementation does not pin a seed for the codebook fit; results may shift across runs until that is fixed.

V12.title: GMM-component tokens (V12)
V12.summary: Global Gaussian Mixture over band intensities; each band emits a token labelled by its dominant component.
V12.theory: Smoother than uniform binning: GMM boundaries flex with the data distribution. Expected to improve F-3 seed stability and F-2 coherence over V1 at a small F-1 classification cost. The smooth boundaries reduce quantisation noise that hurts F-3.

ProdLDA.title: ProdLDA
ProdLDA.summary: Logistic-normal product-of-experts topic model. Already evaluated as a baseline on V1; surfaced here alongside the V-recipes.
ProdLDA.theory: ProdLDA replaces LDA's Dirichlet over topics with a logistic-normal, allowing gradient-based amortised inference. Acts as a deep-learning point of comparison; the V-sweep keeps the existing ProdLDA results untouched and shows them next to the new wordification sweep.

ETM.title: Embedded Topic Model (ETM)
ETM.summary: Topics and words live in a shared embedding space. Already evaluated; surfaced for comparison only.
ETM.theory: ETM jointly learns word embeddings and topic embeddings; the topic-word distribution is the softmax of their dot product. A topology-aware baseline; not re-run per V-recipe in the current sweep.

CAE.title: Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE)
CAE.summary: Non-topic deep baseline. Already evaluated as a representation-learning comparator.
CAE.theory: A convolutional autoencoder over spectra; latent dimensions used as features for the downstream classifier. Surfaced here only as a reference latent-space method.

BetaVAE.title: Beta-VAE
BetaVAE.theory: Beta-VAE encourages factorised latent dimensions via a re-weighted KL term. Like the CAE, this is here for comparison against deep latent-space alternatives, not re-run per recipe.

V13.title: VQ-VAE codebook tokens (V13)
V13.summary: End-to-end learned codebook via VQ-VAE. M=4 sub-vectors, K=32 codewords each. 128-word vocab from gradient-trained quantizer.
V13.theory: V13 trains the wordification end-to-end from the spectrum reconstruction objective. Unlike V11 (k-means PQ) or V12 (statistical GMM), the codebook is gradient-optimised. In practice this *underperforms* handcrafted recipes on F-1 (ranks 13th of 13) because the reconstruction target does not align with classification/coherence. Useful as a design point that shows learned wordifications are not automatically better.

V15.title: Classical RS index tokens (V15)
V15.summary: Per-pixel NDVI/MNDWI/NBR/NDSI/EVI/SAVI quantised to Q bins. Vocab = 6 indices × Q = 48 (or 24 on VNIR-only scenes).
V15.theory: V15 is the classical remote-sensing baseline: hand-crafted vegetation, water, and burn-severity indices, computed per pixel and discretised. Forces reviewers to engage with whether topic models add anything over standard indices. Salinas-A wins F-7 at 0.51 NMI (NDVI cleanly separates crops); other scenes mid-pack.

V14.title: CWT-Morlet tokens (V14)
V14.summary: Continuous wavelet transform with Morlet mother on 16 log-scales × 8 position buckets. Top-16 magnitude cells per pixel. Vocab 1024.
V14.theory: V14 differs from V6 (Db4 DWT level-4) by using *continuous* scales. The Morlet mother gives joint time-frequency localization unlike V6 dyadic scales. F-2 c_v 0.46-0.76 across scenes; competitive with V12 on coherence but distinct on the (scale, position, magnitude) vocabulary.

V16.title: HyperSIGMA foundation-model tokens (V16, scaffold)
V16.summary: Frozen HyperSIGMA embedding of each pixel, quantised via PQ / VQ-VAE / k-means. Vocab depends on codebook (PQ: 256, VQ-VAE: 128, k-means: 200).
V16.theory: V16 uses the TPAMI'25 HyperSIGMA billion-parameter ViT (pre-trained on HyperGlobal-450K) to embed each pixel, then quantises the embedding into LDA tokens. The thesis: a basis learnt on 450K hyperspectral scenes carries discriminative information V1..V15 cannot. **Status (2026-05-28): scaffolded only; weights not vendored; GPU-only in practice.** Highest novelty bet in the V-extension space.

V17.title: Sparse dictionary tokens (V17)
V17.summary: sklearn MiniBatchDictionaryLearning K=64 atoms with LASSO-LARS sparse coding (n_nonzero=8). Vocab 64×Q = 512.
V17.theory: V17 trains an over-complete spectral dictionary then emits one (atom, abundance_bin) token per non-zero coefficient. Generalises V8 endmember unmixing without requiring NFINDR. F-2 c_v 0.34-0.58 — underperforms because per-pixel sparse coding does not align with class structure.

V19.title: UMAP coordinate tokens (V19)
V19.summary: 3D UMAP embedding per scene (n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, seed=42), per-axis percentile-binned. 3 tokens per doc, vocab 24.
V19.theory: V19 reduces each pixel to 3D UMAP coordinates then bins each axis. Abstract tokens carry no spectral semantics — F-2 c_v 0.32-0.41 (low) but F-7 NMI 0.21-0.36 because UMAP separates classes by construction. Documents F-2 / F-7 are NOT measuring the same thing.

V20.title: Mutual-info weighted band tokens (V20)
V20.summary: V1 (band, q-bin) tokens but with copies weighted by per-band mutual information with labels. Up to 8 copies per band per pixel.
V20.theory: V20 takes V1's vocabulary and re-weights each band by its discriminative power (sklearn mutual_info_classif). Bands with high MI emit more copies; near-zero MI bands emit ~none. F-2 c_v 0.74-0.95 — competitive with V12. **V20 wins F-7 NMI on 3 of 5 scenes (indian-pines, salinas-A, kennedy-SC)**, beating V12. The simplest interpretable recipe that beats GMM-token on label-coupling.

V18.title: Graph-Laplacian eigenvector tokens (V18)
V18.summary: k-NN cosine-affinity graph over pixels; first 16 normalised Laplacian eigenvectors per-axis percentile-binned. Vocab 16*Q = 128.
V18.theory: V18 borrows spectral-clustering machinery: build a k-NN affinity graph (k=10), compute the symmetric normalised Laplacian, project pixels onto its 16 smallest-eigenvalue eigenvectors, bin each. F-2 c_v 0.50-0.66 mean ~0.57. F-7 NMI 0.27-0.52 mean ~0.43 (very strong on pavia/salinas-A/salinas). Novel LDA-on-Laplacian framing for HSI.

matrix.lead: Twelve recipes evaluated across three F-axes (F-1 macro-F1, F-2 c_v, F-7 normalised MI). Bold cells = per-axis per-scene winner. The matrix is the headline of the V-sweep: V12 wins F-2 on most scenes and F-7 on 2; V3 wins F-7 on 3; V1 (current canonical) wins F-2 on 2 and F-7 on 0.
